header.subject: Chemistry
header.title: CHEMICAL ANALYSIS – FLAME TESTS & METAL IONS

vocab.definition: the flame colour identifies a metal ion.
NaOH gives coloured precipitates with some ions.

misconceptions.wrong: Two ions in a mix are easy to see by flame.
misconceptions.right: One colour can mask another — a limitation.
Copper is blue, iron(II) green, iron(III) brown.

questions.text: State the flame colour for lithium and potassium. [2 marks]
A flame test gives a yellow flame. Identify the metal ion. [1 mark]
State the precipitate colour when NaOH is added to Cu²⁺ and Fe³⁺. [2 marks]
Explain one limitation of using flame tests on a mixture. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: With NaOH, iron(II) gives a ______ precipitate and iron(III) gives a ______ one.

questions.text: Explain why an insoluble metal hydroxide forms when NaOH is added. [1 mark]

footer.tip: Li crimson, Na yellow, K lilac, Ca orange-red, Cu green.
